To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The Pax2 gene is crucial for specification of the ventrally derived auditory structures and that (ii) the Dlx5, Dlx6 genes are required for specification of the dorsomedially derived vestibular structures.
the Pax2 and Dlx5/6 homeobox transcription factors are crucial for the specification and morphogenesis of auditory and vestibular structures in the vertebrate inner ear, respectively.
Pax2 and Dlx5/Dlx6 homeobox gene activities are crucial for the specification and morphogenesis of distinct inner ear sensory epithelia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of inner ear morphogenetic processes and the identification of genes and signaling cascades involved in the specification of the auditory and vestibular structures.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that control the development of the inner ear.
the identification of inner ear developmental genes and their role in inner ear development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a complex interplay of signaling molecules, transcription factors, and microRNAs are required to orchestrate the development of the inner ear and its distinct components.
inner ear development is controlled by a complex symphony of inner-ear specific transcription factors.
the development and morphogenesis is a symphony of inner-ear developmental control genes and signaling cascades.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a complex and precise temporal and spatially coordinated network of transcriptional regulators, including homeobox genes, secreted factors and MicroRNAs, is required for normal inner ear development and morphogenesis.

the inner ear development is a highly complex process that involves a large number of transcriptional regulators and signaling pathways that are tightly controlled by the inner ear developmental control homeobox genes.

inner ear morphogenesis is a highly complex and well orchestrated process that depends on the precise spatiotemporal expression of a large number of genes, including transcription factors, signaling molecules, and microRNAs.

inner ear morphogenesis is controlled by an intricate network of transcription factors that act in concert with secreted factors, and that the homeobox transcription factors play an essential role in this process.
inner ear development and morphogenesis depends upon a highly coordinated network of genes and their gene products, which interact and regulate each other in complex ways.
the formation of the inner ear is a highly orchestrated and complex process which involves a number of transcription factors and other genes which act together to form this complex organ.
